title: Proposed 48-hour challenge brief: invoice re-entry pilot (scoping draft, not ready to run)

blocks.text: Scope fields supplied by staff; review feasibility, data permission and acceptance before committing.

This brief is for scoping only. It is not ready to run. The synthetic sample is a fictional test and not an actual Kesko project. Owner, production access and acceptance criteria are not yet confirmed. No buyer has agreed to anything.

Could a small, bounded tool reduce duplicate invoice data entry for a fictional process owner, using only the approved 20-invoice CSV, without touching production systems? The goal is to test whether the problem is worth a larger look, not to ship a solution.

Context from the dossier: Kesko's public materials mention an upcoming Q3 2026 interim report (29 Oct 2026) and the Dahl integration, which may create reconciliation work across units. These are reasons to ask, not diagnoses of internal processes.

items.text: Kesko's Q3 2026 interim report is due 29 October 2026.
Integrating Dahl's Nordic technical trade operations, which keep separate brands and units, may require manual reconciliation of order and financial data. Inferred, not confirmed.

blocks.text: 2. Three directions with proposed acceptance tests (all unconfirmed)

rows: Whether a tool can reproduce all 20 approved invoice records
All 20 records copied, zero omissions, every row reviewed by the employee
Whether a guided entry flow reduces staff effort

Time per invoice measured on the sample, compared with a manual baseline. Target to be agreed with the owner. Note: the existing one-week measurement (12h to 8h per week) is self-reported and not a financial result.
Whether mismatches can be surfaced before manual review
Flags raised on a labelled subset of the 20 invoices; precision and recall measured against employee-marked errors

items.text: What is the smallest version a single employee could check in two hours?
Which fields cause most re-keying, and can they be pre-filled from the CSV?
Where do duplicates originate: spreadsheets, email attachments or both?
What would a reviewer need to trust an automated copy?
Which errors are costly enough to flag, and which are noise?
What must remain manual for audit or approval reasons? (Open question for the owner.)

blocks.text: A short demo on the approved 20-invoice CSV only, plus a one-page note listing what was tested, what failed and what remains unknown. No production code.

items.text: No production system or live ERP access.
No outbound messages to Kesko staff or third parties.
No use of data beyond the approved fictional CSV.
No financial savings claims. None were measured.
No commitments on Monday delivery or follow-on work.

rows: Confirm owner, data scope and acceptance test with the process owner
Build the chosen direction against the 20-row CSV
Employee reviews every row; record failures

blocks.text: 7. Proposed staffing (roles only, no names assigned)
One Velho builder, one Velho process analyst, and the named Kesko owner for review. Names and calendar slots are not yet assigned.
Cover note (for Velho employee to review and send manually)

blocks.label: Cover note
blocks.text: We noticed Kesko's Dahl integration and the Q3 report ahead. Could a small, two-day test of invoice re-entry, run only on approved sample data, be worth exploring? Would you be open to a 20-minute scoping call to define the owner, data scope and success test?
